verifications.claim: Toyota is recalling over 550,000 Highlander and Highlander Hybrid SUVs (2021-2024 model years)
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'estimated 550,007 vehicles... 2021 model year through... 2024 model year. Both internal combustion and hybrid'; R2: 'approximately 550,000 Highlander and Highlander Hybrid... 2021 through 2024'; R3: '550,000 Highlander... 2021-2024 Highlander and Highlander Hybrid'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match on number, models, years, and both variants across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The recall is due to a second-row seat defect where the seat back may not lock
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'second-row seat backs... may fail to lock into position'; R2: 'recliner assemblies in the second-row seats may fail to fully lock'; R3: 'recliner assemblies in the second-row seats may not fully lock'
verifications.reasoning: Exact description of the seat back locking defect in all three sources.

verifications.claim: The second-row seat defect increases injury risks
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'greatly increases the risk of injury in the event of a crash'; R2: 'significantly increases the risk of injury'; R3: 'increasing the risk of injury in the event of a crash'
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state increased injury risk due to the defect.

verifications.claim: Dealers will replace the return springs in the seat back recliner assemblies for free
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'replace the return springs in the recliner assemblies. The parts and labor come free'; R2: 'replace the faulty return springs... no cost to the owner'; R3: 'replacing the return springs... free of charge'
verifications.reasoning: Precise match on repair action and free service.

verifications.claim: Owners will be notified by mail starting in April 2026 for the latest recall
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'notified by first-class mail between April 20, 2026, and May 4, 2026'; R2: 'mailing official notification letters... by early May 2026'; R3: 'receive a letter notifying them... next month' (article Mar 2026)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm mail notifications in April/May 2026 timeframe.

verifications.claim: 2021-2024 Highlander/Hybrid (March 2026): Second-row seat back may fail to lock, violating safety standards
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1/R2/R3: 2021-2024 Highlander/Hybrid, 'second-row seat back... may fail to lock'; context implies March 2026 reporting; no explicit 'violating safety standards'
verifications.reasoning: Core details (models, years, defect, timing) directly supported; 'violating safety standards' implied by recall but not explicitly stated.

verifications.claim: 2020-2023 Highlander (Oct 2023): Lower front bumper cover may detach, causing road hazards
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: '2020-2023 models... front lower bumper covers... mounting tabs to detach... could cause a crash' (Oct 27, 2023)
verifications.reasoning: Exact match on years, issue, cause, and date.

verifications.claim: 2024 Grand Highlander (June 2024): Airbag might not deploy correctly if the driver's window is down
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No reference mentions any airbag recall for 2024 Grand Highlander.

verifications.claim: 2017-2019 Highlander: Reports of 8-speed transmission issues, including whining noises and failure
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Toyota Highlander (2017 to present)'... 'high pitched whining noise'... 'complete transmission failure'
verifications.reasoning: Source confirms reports of whining noises and failure for Highlander starting 2017, including specified years.

verifications.claim: Dealers will inspect, install retention hardware, or replace the front bumper cover for the bumper recall
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'inspect... mounting tabs... install retention hardware... replace the upper and lower front bumper cover and install retention hardware'
verifications.reasoning: Precise description of dealer actions for the bumper recall.

verifications.claim: This information is based on reports from March 2026, including data from MotorBiscuit, autoevolution, Fox Business, and USA Today
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1 (autoevolution), R2 (MotorBiscuit), R3 (Fox8, Mar 12, 2026) match recent context; R5 (USA Today, Oct 2023) contradicts March 2026 date
verifications.reasoning: Sources match listed sites (Fox affiliate for Fox Business), most align with March 2026 context for seat recall, but USA Today report dated 2023 creates date mismatch.
